title: Diarrhea

rationale.Colonoscopy + biopsy: Skip lesions, cobblestoning, transmural inflammation, non-caseating granulomas.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with chronic diarrhea (often non-bloody), RLQ abdominal pain, weight loss, fatigue, and fever. Crohn's disease is a transmural granulomatous inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the GI tract from mouth to anus — most commonly terminal ileum. Skip lesions (areas of inflammation between normal mucosa), cobblestoning, creeping fat, strictures, and fistulas are characteristic. Extraintestinal manifestations: arthritis, uveitis, erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum, PSC. Diagnosis: colonoscopy with terminal ileum intubation and biopsy (transmural inflammation, non-caseating granulomas). CT/MR enterography for small bowel evaluation. Labs: anemia, elevated CRP/ESR, fecal calprotectin. Treatment: mild-mod → budesonide (terminal ileal/right colon) or prednisone for induction. Maintenance: immunomodulators (azathioprine, MTX), biologics (anti-TNF — infliximab, adalimumab). Surgery for complications (strictures, fistulas, abscess) — NOT curative (disease recurs).
